sources.entry: Send | Simple, private, end-to-end encrypted file sharing

summary.one_liner: A community-maintained fork of Mozilla's discontinued Firefox Send, a web app for sending end-to-end encrypted files to other people.
summary.what_it_does: A web application for uploading files and sharing them with others through a link, with the files encrypted end-to-end. It is a fork of Mozilla's Firefox Send, with Mozilla and Firefox branding removed and dependencies updated. The fork stays compatible with the ffsend command-line client. The README describes server configuration through environment variables (see server/config.js), optional Redis and AWS S3 or compatible storage, and Docker and AWS deployment guides. It also has a Localization guide and a list of public instances. Development uses npm scripts for starting a dev server, building production assets, running mocha tests, and linting. Android client code lives in the repository's android directory. The README does not describe the internals of the encryption scheme beyond calling it end-to-end encrypted.
use_cases: Self-host a private file sharing site for your organization
Send encrypted files to someone without a shared account
Share large files via a temporary link
Run a Send instance on Docker
Use the ffsend command line tool to upload and download files
Store uploaded files in AWS S3 or a compatible service
notable: Community fork of Mozilla's Firefox Send, which Mozilla discontinued, with branding removed so it can be self-hosted
Kept compatible with the ffsend command-line client
Selectively merged some of Mozilla's later changes from the experimental v4 branch
Optional Redis and S3 backends, configured through environment variables
Includes an Android client in the android directory and a FileLink provider for Thunderbird
caveats: Mozilla's report feature, download tokens, trust warnings and FxA changes are not included in this fork
Mozilla discontinued the original project, so this fork depends on community maintenance
The README describes it as a file sharing experiment
